headline: Failed House rule would have set debate terms for bills on firearms laws, undersea cables in marine sanctuaries, and critical energy minerals.
what_it_does: This resolution was a procedural "rule" that would have set the terms for the House to debate and vote on three bills. One bill, H.R. 2189, would update federal firearms laws to account for new technology and less-than-lethal weapons. Another, H.R. 261, would stop agencies from requiring a new permit for undersea fiber optic cables in national marine sanctuaries if a federal or state agency already approved them. The third, H.R. 3617, would direct the Department of Energy to secure supplies of critical minerals and other energy materials. The rule itself would not have changed any law; it only would have allowed the House to take up these bills.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives
who_it_affects.how: They would have debated and voted on the three bills under the time limits and rules this resolution set.
